instruction:
Rename Armature Bones to Restore Skinning `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend`
contains an armature object `Rig` with a 4-bone parent chain, but the bones
were imported with the same generic base name. `Skin` has vertex groups
named `Bone.Root`, `Bone.A`, `Bone.B`, and `Bone.Tip`, so the armature must
be renamed along the actual root-to-tip chain for the skinning to work.

## Requirements
1. `Rig` is an armature with exactly 4 bones.
2. The bone names are exactly `{Bone.Root, Bone.A, Bone.B, Bone.Tip}`.
3. The parent chain is `Bone.Root -> Bone.A -> Bone.B -> Bone.Tip`.
4. `Skin` is a mesh with an Armature modifier pointing to `Rig`.
5. `Skin`'s vertex groups are exactly the four semantic names above.
6. Every vertex-group name resolves to a bone on `Rig`.

Do not add, remove, or reparent bones; only rename them by walking the
chain from root to tip. Save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal.
